articles.title: Marsh Landing Gets $48,000 for Bike Repair Clinic
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in September.
body: The Marsh Landing Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
The group has raised $48,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Tuesday mornings.
Julia Hartigan, who has lived in Marsh Landing for 30 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. Public works estimates the work will take about 30 weeks once it begins.

body: Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Monday mornings. Nelson Vance, who has lived in Tannery Flats for 8 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

articles.title: Letter: Thanks to the Kettle Hill Block Association
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the November meeting. Please keep the Saturday cleanup day in the budget. Many of us on Willow Street use it every week.
Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
To the editor: I have lived on Willow Street for 9 years, and I want to say what a difference the Kettle Hill Block Association has made.
Albert Murphy, Eastgate

articles.title: Plans for Community Garden Set for Mill Hill This Spring
articles.deck: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public.
body: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public. Organizers ask guests to bring a dish to share or a little cash for supplies.
The event will be held at the Bellwood Chapel, rain or shine, with a backup date set for the following Saturday. Children are welcome, and volunteers will be on hand to help with parking and set-up.

articles.title: Briar Terrace Repaving Set to Begin in December
articles.deck: Residents of Upper Commons met on Thursday to talk over the plan.
body: Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at Millrace Green on Thursday at 7 p.m.
The effort began in December when a handful of neighbors met at Millrace Green to talk about crosswalk.
Several residents on Briar Terrace said they had been waiting since 1974 for something like this.

articles.title: Budget Hearing Draws 13 Residents
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Keystone Terrace disagreed about cost and timing.
body: Residents of Lower Millrace said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street. Councilmember Hannah Thibodeaux asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $1,200.
Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days. Public works estimates the work will take about 13 weeks once it starts in April.

articles.title: Alma Bruckner, 67, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Alma Bruckner for the many years of service to Bellwood.
body: Alma Bruckner died in October at home on Chapel Lane, at the age of 67.
Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Bellwood.

articles.title: Then & Now: the Cedar Hollow Pavilion, 1977 and 2013
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: A 1977 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Laurel Street from the corner of Juniper Street. Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.
Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal.

articles.title: Hickory Ridge Elementary Students Earn Regional Honors
articles.deck: The program begins in May and is open to all students in grade 3 and up.
body: The board will review the results at the end of the spring term. Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for May.

Students will meet on Monday afternoons in Millrace Green, and transportation will be provided for those who need it. Principal Brian Varga said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers.
The board will review the results at the end of the spring term.
